places.now: Ratcliff, a district of Tower Hamlets between Limehouse and Shadwell, on the north bank of the Thames

places.now: Reading, Berkshire; town centre near the station and Forbury
places.reason: Reading is a well-known market town on the Bath Road coach route; the gazetteer matched a hospital instead of the town centre.

places.now: Southampton city centre, Hampshire, near the Old Town and docks
places.reason: Southampton was a major port and the terminus of the London and South Western Railway from 1840; the gazetteer's guess is a suburban street, not the town centre.

places.now: Fictional inn; often associated with the Horseshoe and Castle at Cooling or pubs in Upnor and Gravesend, none with proof

places.now: Tooting, in the London Borough of Wandsworth (Tooting Bec and Tooting Graveney)
places.reason: Tooting was a Surrey village then, now south-west London; the coordinates are the centre of Tooting.

places.now: High Barnet, in the London Borough of Barnet, on the A1000 Great North Road
places.reason: Barnet was a coaching stop on the Great North Road, with the main town at High Barnet; the gazetteer matched only a road.

places.now: Fictional house; the 'Boffin's Bower' is a composite, and the mansion near Cavendish Square/Marylebone has no known surviving building
places.reason: Boffin's house is described as a large mansion in a fashionable area of the West End (Cavendish Square/Marylebone) but is a fictional house, so this is a loose district guess.

places.now: The Borough area around Borough High Street, Southwark; London Bridge/Borough Market
places.reason: The Borough means the Southwark district around Borough High Street, where the gazetteer's match is appropriate.

places.now: Chatham, Kent, around the High Street and the Historic Dockyard
places.reason: Chatham was an important naval dockyard town on the Medway; the gazetteer matched a school in a suburb rather than the town centre.

places.now: Fictional; likely the area around Leadenhall Street/Cornhill, City of London; no surviving building

places.now: Historical region of South and Southeast Asia (India through the Malay Archipelago); not a single place

places.now: Demolished; the site lies under Holborn Viaduct and Farringdon Road near Saffron Hill
places.reason: Field Lane was a notorious slum and handkerchief-fence street running from Holborn Hill to Saffron Hill beside the Fleet River; it was cleared in the 1840s-1870s for the Holborn Viaduct and Farringdon Road.

places.now: Demolished 1827; site near Charing Cross station and Trafalgar Square (the Golden Cross Hotel/Pub Craven Street survives nearby)
places.reason: The Golden Cross coaching inn stood at Charing Cross near the Strand; it was rebuilt, and then demolished in the 1850s when Charing Cross Station was extended.

places.now: Great St Bernard Hospice, at the Swiss-Italian border pass (Switzerland, Valais), still operating
places.reason: The hospice of the Great St Bernard Pass stands at about 2,470 m on the Swiss-Italian border.

places.now: Hoo Peninsula and Cliffe/Cooling marshes on the Thames estuary, north Kent
places.reason: Dickens's marsh country is based on the Thames-Medway marshes near Cooling and Higham, so this is a regional point.

places.now: Fictional; the setting is in the Chancery Lane/Cursitor Street area, with no surviving building

places.now: Part of Limehouse by the Thames, around Narrow Street and Limehouse Basin, Tower Hamlets
places.reason: Limehouse Hole was the riverside stretch of Limehouse near Narrow Street, west of the Regent's Canal Dock; the exact boundary is imprecise.

places.now: Liverpool city centre, Merseyside
places.reason: Liverpool was a major port; the gazetteer matched a canal branch instead of the city.

places.now: Millbank on the north bank of the Thames, Westminster, near the Tate Britain and Lambeth Bridge
places.reason: Millbank is the riverside street running south from the Houses of Parliament; the Millbank Penitentiary (now Tate Britain) was nearby.

places.now: Restoration House, Crow Lane, Rochester, which is the main model for Satis House (Satis House itself is on Satis Avenue)
places.reason: Satis House is fictional but modelled on Restoration House (and the real Satis House) in Rochester, Kent.

places.now: Demolished; the site was at Hungerford Stairs, now beneath Charing Cross station area, near Embankment
